industry.beds: India has ~16 hospital beds per 10,000 people vs a global average of ~33, and ~14 outside the metros; only ~6% of hospitals are accredited (Crisil, Praxis, via Fortis AR FY26 MD&A).
industry.insurance: Health-insurance coverage rose from 35% (FY2019) to 41% (FY2024) of the population (Crisil, IRDA); 36% of Fortis's FY26 hospital revenue came through insurers (TPAs) and ~21% from government schemes (CGHS, ECHS, PSUs).
industry.diagnostics: Indian diagnostics market ₹860-870 bn in FY24, projected ₹1,275-1,375 bn by FY28 (10-12% a year; Crisil, Axis Capital); still fragmented, with organised chains (Dr Lal, Metropolis, Agilus, Vijaya, Apollo, Redcliffe and online players) gaining share.
industry.src: Fortis AR FY26 MD&A pp.188-193 (Crisil, Praxis, IRDA, Axis Capital)
themes: Demand for tertiary care in Fortis's metros (NCR, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Kolkata, Punjab) keeps occupancy ~68-70% even as beds grow 15-17%.
TPAs are 36-37% of hospital revenue; insured patients choose branded chains, but insurers also push back on tariffs.
~21% of revenue. CGHS raised package rates in FY26 but capped chemotherapy drugs at MRP less 30%: Fortis's oncology growth fell from 23-24% to ~5%.

On 29-Sep-2026 the Supreme Court called hospital cancer-drug mark-ups 'carnage' and asked the Centre whether a uniform 16% margin on MRP could be an option. Not a ruling yet; hospital stocks fell 4-7% on 30-Sep-2026 (Fortis −5.2% in morning trade). Pharmacy is a large profit pool for every hospital chain; Fortis does not disclose its pharmacy revenue.
New supply in NCR and Bengaluru
Large new hospitals in Noida and Gurugram caused doctor churn (management, Aug-2026); BG Road Bengaluru runs at ~55% occupancy against a larger competitor next door.
International patients 7.5-7.8% of hospital revenue (₹639 cr in FY26, +18.5%), but growth slowed to 11-13% in Q4FY26-Q1FY27 (Bangladesh, travel).
Agilus grew 4% a year in FY23-26 vs a 10-12% market; online aggregators and hospital-led labs compete on price.

moat: Brand and clinical depth
Moderate advantage
FMRI Gurugram (₹1,137 cr revenue, ~85-90% occupancy, ARPOB ~₹4.7 cr) and FEHI are national referral centres; 4 JCI hospitals; 62% of revenue from high-end specialties.
Pricing power in flagship units, not network-wide.
Cluster density
Advantage in NCR and Punjab
~2,190 beds in NCR and ~990 in Punjab; brownfield beds fill 'immediately' (Faridabad, Noida).
Cheap growth: brownfield beds earn more than new hospitals.
Asset quality and returns
Weak
ROCE ~13% (FY26) on a base with ₹4,722 cr of goodwill; 6 of 24 facilities below 15% margin; BG Road at ~55% occupancy.
Returns barely above the ~11.6% cost of capital.
Doctor model
No advantage
Visiting/fee-for-service doctors like most peers; new ESOP (₹150 cr in FY27) to stop poaching in NCR.
Doctors, not the brand, own many patient relationships.
Diagnostics (Agilus)
Weakened
A national pathology network (4,493 touchpoints, 40.8 mn tests), but growth 4% a year FY23-26 vs 10-12% for the market; new CEO from Jul-2026.
Scale without share gains; valued below listed peers.
Parent (IHH)
Mixed
IHH brings capital, procurement and governance; it also controls the Gleneagles assets Fortis may buy or merge with.
Support for growth, but related-party terms matter.

gaps: Hospital-level EBITDA is disclosed only in margin bands (the margin matrix); cohort occupancy and ARPOB are band averages and the facilities in each band change every quarter. Our mature/ramp-up/new-bed cohorts use the Q1FY27 bands.

Fortis does not disclose ALOS, inpatient vs outpatient revenue split by value (OPD is ~14% of the specialty mix), pharmacy revenue, EBITDA per bed or capex per bed; the Q1FY27 ALOS (4.19 days) comes from a broker note.
ARPOB is on gross revenue; the company does not reconcile it to reported revenue. Our 0.945 conversion is derived (FY25-Q1FY27).
Revenue from the FY26 acquisitions (Jalandhar, Greater Noida, People Tree) is given only once (~₹72 cr in Q4FY26 for TMI, Adayu and Jalandhar); organic growth for FY26 and Q1FY27 is our estimate.

Bed-addition timing by project is not disclosed beyond the yearly totals in the bed plan (FY27 472, FY28 173, FY29 702, FY30 429) and the FMRI/Shalimar Bagh/Mohali/Amritsar comments; average beds in operation are our estimate.
Agilus net cash/debt and standalone balance sheet were not read; the minority deduction treats Agilus equity ≈ EV.
Market values of the associates (Lanka Hospitals 28.6%, RHT 27.8%) not computed; carried at book (~₹225 cr).
ICICI Securities, Nomura, Geojit and Axis Direct estimates (EBITDA, EPS) are not public; Nomura's method not known. JP Morgan and Citi notes not found.
Exact years of pre-2016 corporate history (listing, Escorts and SRL acquisitions, RHT sale-and-leaseback) not verified in filings read for this report.
CRISIL rating rationale of 9-Sep-2026 not read (rating level not used).
Jefferies' reported estimate of the EBITDA hit from a drug-margin cap could not be verified from an accessible source; not used.
Gleneagles India financials (revenue ~₹70 cr a month per the CFO, May-2026) and any merger valuation are not available.
Daiichi award size differs by source (₹2,562 cr in LiveLaw, Sep-2026; ~₹3,500 cr award and ~₹5,300 cr outstanding in other press); award year (2016) per press, not filings read.
